players.product: AI-accelerated modeling and simulation software for drug development

quarterly_data.signal: CEO Shawn O'Connor on the regulatory and demand backdrop: market conditions remain encouraging globally, supported by ongoing most favored nation pricing agreements, easing tariff concerns and a more supportive funding environment for customers; on the regulatory front, the new approach methodologies (NAMs) guidance issued late last year was further clarified with an additional update last month, and the company is seeing a pickup in client spending reflected in solid software renewal rates, increased new logo activity and strength in service bookings. In Q&A he said the NAM-driven momentum is on the horizon but still a couple of years out, that regulatory support for biosimulation, in silico methodologies and AI is broadly strong, and that the company is still operating in an environment where 'fragile might be a reasonable term', with macro issues around global politics and more specific pharma-related scenarios, which drives a cautious approach to guidance.

CEO on the clinical-operations and commercialization businesses that came with the Pro-ficiency acquisition: the medical communications services business is up nicely through the halfway point of the year after a very good first quarter, with lower percentage growth in the second quarter; Pro-ficiency software revenue stepped back in the back half of 2025 as clinical trial activity fell, continued at that run rate into the first half of fiscal 2026, has now stabilized, and management looks for reasonable growth for Pro-ficiency from this point forward. He said the Pro-ficiency acquisition opened the company's reach into clients' clinical trial operation budgets.
